Interview Experience 
 
 
 
 
Eligibility Criteria: 7+ CPI & more than 70% in 10th and 12th. 
Stipend: 40,000 
Branch: Computer Engineering, Information Technology 
 
Round 1: Coding Round (23rd November 4.00pm) 
This was an Offline assessment round where we need to solve 41 questions in total 
on Hackerrank platform at TPO seminar hall and some invigilator from UBS would be 
present there. Time limit was 75 minutes. 
41 questions consisted of 20 MCQs of JAVA, DBMS, OOPs, etc, 20 MCQs of 
Reasoning/aptitude type and 1 coding question. 
The coding question was as follows- You are given an arraylist of spam_words and an 
arraylist of email subjects. An email can be considered as spam if it contains more than 
2 spam words. Even if one spam word is repeated, it will be counted as two. Also, you 
need to ensure that it is case insensitive. 
Eg:  
INPUT 
spam_words = [“free”, “prize”, “Lottery”, “win”] 
email_subjects = [“click link to win lottery”, “Leetcode weekly digest”]  
OUTPUT:

spam 
not_spam 
Note that in first email subject “lottery” and “Lottery” casing is different, so we need to 
also add checks to match those. Therefore, you should know about String in-built 
functions.  
Using Brute Force method, I was able to pass 10/15 testcases. 
Interview shortlisting was announced on 24th Nov and 8 students were selected for 
virtual interviews. 
Round 2: Virtual Interview (29th November) 
The interview was conducted on Microsoft Teams and it went for around 45-50 minutes. 
There were 2 persons. One of them asked technical questions and the other one asked 
HR questions.  
It all starts with Introduce yourself question which you must be prepared with. 
Next, she asked about my projects which I had mentioned on my resume and this leads 
to some follow-up questions like ‘Why did u use React’ then she asked me about HTML, 
what is the general structure in html, what is a stylesheet, how do we link a CSS file to 
an html file, why is JS needed, etc, which were some pretty basic questions. 
Then she moved onto DBMS and OOPs in which she asked about some SQL queries, 
what is normalization, what is 2NF and in oops she asked why do we use OOPs, then 
what is data encapsulation and abstraction. Give name of 4 languages that uses OOPs. 
Now she started reading my resume and asked what is Linear Algebra (I had mentioned 
linear algebra in my coursework section) which was totally unexpected becoz 
interviewer usually asks about dbms, oops and os. So, I replied that it has eigen values 
and eigen vectors which are used in ML field. I know that isn’t the full answer but it 
wasn’t wrong. Moving on to the skills section she asked what is GitHub and GitLab, how 
to connect local repo to remote repo (using git clone command, or git remote add origin 
command), can we connect our local repo to more than one remote repo (Yes, we can 
by using command git remote add <another remote repo name>), what does ‘git 
remote’ command do, etc 
She also asked a puzzle: Minimum number of cuts required to pay salary from N length 
Gold Bar - GeeksforGeeks 
At first, I did not understand what I had to do so I asked the interviewer for clarification 
and then still I could not think of any approach so I just started speaking out my 
thoughts and then with a little help from them I solved it. 
HR questions- 
1. What do you know about UBS?

2. How did you complete so many mini projects along with college work 
3. What are your short terms and long-term goals? 
4. If we want to hire an employee for work-from-home job, what qualities or 
characteristics he should possess? 
Results were announced the same day and 5 candidates were selected including me. 
TIPS: 
• Read previous year experiences provided by COC and/or GFG archives. With 
the help of this I knew that UBS generally doesn’t ask much related to OS hence I 
skipped revising OS. 
• Always be prepared with all common HR questions and try to blend your 
answers with company’s principles or values.  
• If you are stuck in some DSA/puzzle question, just speak out your thoughts so 
that interviewer might help you to solve. 
• Whenever the interviewer asks you a question, make sure that you understand 
the question correctly and I would suggest that you repeat whatever you 
understand again so that the interviewer can repeat the question again if you 
misunderstand something. 
• Be prepared to answer questions related to every thing you have written on your 
resume. Everything. 
• Answer any OOPs questions by relating it with real-world scenarios. 
• Understand the motive behind interviewer asking a certain question and answer 
accordingly. 
RESOURCES: 
I had prepared OOPs, DBMS, OS and Java interview questions from InterviewBit and 
notes from GFG.
